newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan central bank governor gets second term. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pakistan central bank governor gets second term. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]

text.p: State (central) Bank of Pakistan governor Muhammad Yaqub was reappointed by the caretaker government for a second term, the official APP news agency reported on Wednesday.
APP said the Finance Ministry had announced that Yaqub's second term would begin on February 14.

Yaqub, a former official of the International Monetary Fund, was first appointed central bank governor in 1993 by then-prime minister Nawaz Sharif. (Corrects name and description of appointing authority.)
APP did not say how long Yaqub's second term would last. The normal tenure for a central bank governor is three years.
Yaqub's reappointment came just five days before Pakistan is due to vote in national and provincial elections.
